Standard table of weather station data

Source: R/io-weather.R
ef_station_table.Rd

Builds the standard station table of EarthFlux: the metadata of the weather stations (stations, one row per station) and their observations (observations, one row per station and timestamp), joined by station_id, together with the provenance of the data. The constructor normalises the inputs (plain data frames, timestamps in UTC, declared unit conversions), removes exact duplicated records and validates the contract. It never guesses units or time zones and never corrects values: impossible metadata are errors, while impossible or suspicious observations are kept and flagged by ef_station_qc().

Usage

ef_station_table(
  stations,
  observations,
  provenance,
  units = NULL,
  timestamp_format = NULL,
  tz = NULL
)

Arguments

stations

A data frame with one row per station. Required columns: station_id (character, unique, not missing), lon and lat (decimal degrees, WGS84; longitude in [-180, 180], east positive; latitude in [-90, 90], north positive) and elevation (finite, m above sea level). Conditionally required: height_wind (anemometer height [m above ground], > 0.0947 m, the domain of FAO-56 Eq. 47) when observations has wind_speed, and height_temp_rh (height of the temperature and humidity sensors [m above ground], > 0) when observations has any temperature or humidity variable. Heights may be NA (unknown); such records are flagged by ef_station_qc(). Optional columns: surface_type (one of "reference_grass", "reference_alfalfa", "irrigated_other", "non_reference", "unknown"; stored as a factor), and the character columns network, provider, license, terms_url, name and notes. Other columns are rejected.

observations

A data frame with one row per station and timestamp. Required columns: station_id (character, present in stations) and timestamp (POSIXct with an explicit time zone, or character with timestamp_format and tz), plus at least one measured variable. Measured variables (numeric; contract units): air_temperature [degC], relative_humidity [%], dewpoint_temperature [degC], vapour_pressure [kPa], wind_speed [m s-1] (at height_wind), solar_radiation [W m-2] (global irradiance on a horizontal plane, mean of the period), air_pressure [kPa], precipitation [mm], net_radiation [W m-2], and for daily data tmax, tmin [degC], rh_max, rh_min [%]. Missing values are allowed. Other columns are rejected.

provenance

A named list describing the data. Required fields: timestamp_convention ("end", "start" or "instant": whether the timestamp marks the end or the start of the averaging period, or an instantaneous value), interval (time step of the records in seconds, a positive whole number, e.g. 3600) and crs (the coordinate reference system of lon/lat; must be "EPSG:4326"). Recommended fields: source (file, URL or API), retrieved (date of download or reading), source_hash, network, provider, license. Any other named field is kept; the fields source_tz, units, duplicates_removed, package_version, operations, qc, flags and flags_evaluated are reserved (set by the package).

units

NULL (all variables already in contract units) or a named list (or named character vector) declaring the source unit of some measured variables, which are then converted to the contract unit and recorded in the provenance. Accepted declarations: temperatures "degC" or "K"; humidities "%" or "fraction"; pressures "kPa", "hPa" or "Pa"; wind_speed "m/s" or "km/h"; radiation "W/m2", "MJ/m2/h" or "MJ/m2/d" (rates); precipitation "mm".

timestamp_format, tz

Only for character timestamps, and then both required (no default): the format passed to as.POSIXct() (e.g. "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") and the IANA time zone of the strings (e.g. "UTC", "Etc/GMT+4", "America/Santiago"; see OlsonNames()).

Value

An object of class c("earthflux_station_table", "list") with elements:

  • stations: data frame of the stations, with the columns supplied (surface_type as a factor with the five levels above);

  • observations: data frame of the records, in the order supplied (exact duplicates removed), timestamp as POSIXct in UTC and the measured variables as double in contract units;

  • provenance: the list supplied plus source_tz (time zone of the input timestamps), units (data frame variable, source_unit, unit, scale, offset), duplicates_removed (number of exact duplicated records removed), package_version and operations (a data frame log with columns step and detail);

  • qc: the long audit table of quality control flags, with zero rows until ef_station_qc() is run (columns described there);

  • flags: an empty list of diagnostic flag records.

Details

Time (dev/specs/weather-forcing.md section 2.4). Timestamps are stored as POSIXct in UTC. A POSIXct input must carry an explicit time zone (a non-empty tzone attribute); character input is parsed with the declared timestamp_format and tz, and any string that does not parse (including local times that do not exist because of a daylight saving change) is an error. Local times that occur twice at the end of daylight saving time are resolved by as.POSIXct(); to avoid the ambiguity give UTC or a fixed-offset zone such as "Etc/GMT+4". For averages over a period the mid-point is timestamp - interval / 2 ("end") or timestamp + interval / 2 ("start"); FAO-56 Eq. 31 uses the time at the mid-point of the period.

Duplicates. Records with the same station_id and timestamp and identical values are kept once and counted in provenance$duplicates_removed; duplicates with different values are an error (they are never averaged).

Domain. Impossible metadata are errors of class earthflux_domain_error: coordinates out of range, non-finite elevation, heights at or below their bound. Infinite observed values are also errors. Physically impossible observations (e.g. a negative relative humidity) are not errors here: they are kept and flagged with severity critical by ef_station_qc() (decision WF-04), so that one record does not stop a long series.

Errors. All errors inherit earthflux_input_error. Specific classes: earthflux_station_field_error (missing, unknown or mistyped field, zero rows, missing value in a required field), earthflux_station_time_error (timestamp without explicit time zone, unparsable timestamp, invalid timestamp_convention or interval), earthflux_station_unknown_id (observations of a station not in stations), earthflux_station_duplicate (duplicated station_id in stations, or duplicated records with different values), earthflux_station_provenance_error (provenance not a named list, missing or unsupported crs, reserved fields) and earthflux_domain_error.

Not covered yet: readers for the files or services of specific networks (their access, licences, time zones and sensor heights are open items, dev/specs/weather-forcing.md section 9) and the vertical datum of the elevation.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

See also

ef_station_qc() for the quality control of the table.

Examples

# A tiny synthetic data set (fictitious stations).
stations <- data.frame(
  station_id = c("ST01", "ST02"),
  lon = c(-71.50, -71.20), lat = c(-35.40, -35.10),
  elevation = c(150, 420),
  height_wind = c(2, 10), height_temp_rh = c(2, 2)
)
times <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-15 13:00", tz = "UTC") + 3600 * 0:2
observations <- data.frame(
  station_id = rep(c("ST01", "ST02"), each = 3),
  timestamp = rep(times, 2),
  air_temperature = c(24.1, 25.3, 26.0, 21.8, 22.9, 23.5),
  relative_humidity = c(45, 41, 38, 52, 48, 46),
  wind_speed = c(2.1, 2.6, 3.0, 3.4, 3.9, 4.1)
)
st <- ef_station_table(
  stations, observations,
  provenance = list(timestamp_convention = "end", interval = 3600,
                    crs = "EPSG:4326", source = "synthetic example")
)
st
#> <earthflux_station_table>
#> Stations: 2 (coordinates EPSG:4326)
#> Records: 6, 2024-01-15 13:00:00 to 2024-01-15 15:00:00 UTC (source time zone: UTC)
#> Time step: 3600 s; timestamps mark the end of each period
#> Variables: air_temperature [degC], relative_humidity [%], wind_speed [m/s] 
#> Quality control: not run (see ef_station_qc())

# Declared conversion: wind speed recorded in km/h.
obs_kmh <- observations
obs_kmh$wind_speed <- obs_kmh$wind_speed * 3.6
st2 <- ef_station_table(
  stations, obs_kmh,
  provenance = list(timestamp_convention = "end", interval = 3600,
                    crs = "EPSG:4326"),
  units = list(wind_speed = "km/h")
)
st2$provenance$units
#>            variable source_unit unit     scale offset
#> 1   air_temperature        degC degC 1.0000000      0
#> 2 relative_humidity           %    % 1.0000000      0
#> 3        wind_speed        km/h  m/s 0.2777778      0
